explanation: Catholic countries jumped straight from Thursday 4 October to Friday 15 October 1582, skipping 10 days to bring Easter back in line with the March equinox.

claims.text: The Gregorian calendar is named after Pope Gregory XIII, who introduced it in 1582.
Gregory I, Julius II and Sixtus V did not introduce the Gregorian calendar; Sixtus V was Gregory XIII's successor.
In Catholic countries, Thursday 4 October 1582 was followed by Friday 15 October 1582.
The reform aimed to bring the date of Easter back in line with the March equinox.

issues.note: c3 and the explanation say Catholic countries jumped straight from Thursday 4 October to Friday 15 October 1582. Only the first adopters did (Spain, Portugal, most Italian states, Poland-Lithuania). France went from 9 to 20 December 1582, and the Catholic German states, Austria and Hungary switched between 1583 and 1587. Suggest 'Spain, Portugal and most of Italy jumped straight from...' or 'The first countries to switch jumped straight from...', with c3 reworded to match.
